summary:
VitalOrbit is a real-time astronaut health monitoring and early warning web application developed by Team Agro Builds for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It combines camera-based body tracking using MediaPipe Pose with simulated biometric sensor readings to monitor astronauts during exercise. The system tracks body posture, joint angles, repetitions, exercise quality, heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, respiration rate, and blood glucose.

VitalOrbit establishes personal health baselines, detects abnormal readings, and generates three levels of alerts: Info, Caution, and Critical, along with recommended actions. It also includes a Ground Control dashboard where flight surgeons can monitor health trends and receive alerts from space through a simulated store-and-forward communication system that accounts for delays and connectivity interruptions.

By connecting astronaut self-monitoring with Earth-based medical support, VitalOrbit addresses the health risks of long-duration space missions, including microgravity, isolation, and hostile environments. Its goal is to support early risk detection, informed decisions, and safer human space exploration.
details:
Project Details – VitalOrbit

VitalOrbit is a smart astronaut health monitoring and early warning system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It combines computer vision, biometric health monitoring, intelligent alert generation, and a Ground Control dashboard to help detect potential health risks early.

1. How Does It Work?

VitalOrbit uses a camera and MediaPipe Pose estimation to track an astronaut's body movements during exercise. It measures joint angles, counts repetitions, monitors exercise tempo, checks left-right symmetry, and calculates a form-quality score. If the camera is unavailable, a simulated skeleton provides a demonstration mode.

The application also displays biometric readings such as heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, body temperature, respiration rate, blood glucose, and body mass. Simulated sensor data is used to demonstrate the monitoring system.

During the initial 30 seconds, the application establishes personal health baselines. It compares subsequent readings against these baselines and predefined safety thresholds. When an abnormal condition is detected, it generates Info, Caution, or Critical alerts with recommended actions and NASA spaceflight hazard tags.

An alert packet containing the astronaut's health snapshot, timestamp, recent trends, and recommended action is transmitted to the Ground Control dashboard. A store-and-forward system simulates communication delays between Earth, the Moon, and Mars. If communication is interrupted, alerts remain queued until the connection is restored.

2. Benefits of the Project

  • Continuous monitoring of astronaut health during exercise.
  • Early identification of unusual health patterns and potential risks.
  • Improved exercise posture and movement quality through real-time feedback.
  • Personalized monitoring using individual health baselines.
  • Faster communication of critical health information to Ground Control.
  • Reliable alert delivery simulation during communication interruptions.
  • Easy-to-understand visual dashboards for astronauts and flight surgeons.

3. Intended Impact

VitalOrbit aims to improve astronaut safety and support medical decision-making during long-duration missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. It addresses health risks associated with microgravity, isolation, hostile environments, and other spaceflight hazards.

The system is designed to help astronauts monitor their own health while allowing Earth-based medical teams to identify concerning trends and provide timely guidance, even when communication is delayed.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript / React (as applicable to the implementation).
  • Computer Vision: MediaPipe Pose for real-time human body tracking.
  • Health Monitoring: Simulated biometric sensor data and threshold-based detection.
  • Data Visualization: Dynamic charts, health indicators, and monitoring dashboards.
  • Communication Simulation: Store-and-forward alert queue with simulated Earth-Moon-Mars communication delays.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, web browser, and Git/GitHub (as applicable).

5. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation of VitalOrbit is its integration of exercise analysis, health monitoring, and space communication simulation into a single platform. Instead of simply displaying vital signs, it connects physical performance with health-risk detection and recommended actions.

Its personalized baseline system, three-level alert mechanism, NASA hazard tagging, simulated microgravity mass measurement, and communication-delay simulation make it relevant to the unique challenges of human space exploration.

6. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered:

  • The five major NASA spaceflight hazards.
  • The limited availability of medical assistance during space missions.
  • Communication delays and temporary loss of connectivity.
  • The importance of astronaut self-monitoring.
  • Individual differences in health measurements.
  • Simple, readable interfaces for quick decision-making.
  • The need for a camera-independent demonstration mode.
  • Data privacy, reliability, and the importance of avoiding false alarms.

Overall, VitalOrbit aims to make astronaut health monitoring more accessible, intelligent, and responsive, contributing to safer and more sustainable human exploration of space.
